comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh permitted revisit: the public 2026–2027 bachelor study guide identifies BSc Clinical Technology (B-KT), programme32106, 180EC, with 26 taught components totalling150EC plus the formally required30EC minor. Its current KT2755 course32312 explicitly belongs to this bachelor as well as the separate master bridge and assigns3.5EC. This is genuine current bachelor evidence, no longer merely an inference from the MSc bridge. However, the adopted BSc OER effective31August2026 still assigns KT2755 4.5EC in Appendix3, while Article7 specifies180EC overall; its printed course allocation totals181EC. Article7(4) locates course weights in the OER appendix and7(5) describes the guide as elaborating actual teaching. Under Production Instructions2.1 formal-source precedence, the catalogue is not treated as an explicit amendment to that conflicting adopted weight. The current bachelor examination rules retain the30ECminor for entrants from2024–2025 but supply no placement-credit correction or credit-sharing rule. Preserve the 27OER components as diagnostic181EC and display only the unchanged verified first-year60EC. Placement requiresKT1905/equivalent and vaccination; KT2905 requiresKT1905; KT3905 requiresKT1905 andKT2905; KTO requires all60first-yearEC plus at least53second-yearEC and project/proposal approvals. The current catalogue is accessible through its public programme and course entries; an older linked entry404 is not the academic blocker. Complete reconstruction and dependent UCR approval remain withheld pending authoritative reconciliation of current BSc sources.

audience.programmeDescription: Clinical Technology combines medicine and engineering to study the human body, disease and medical technology. The joint programme includes integrated medical and technical subjects, clinical and communication skills, design work, a healthcare placement and a research or design capstone.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine substantial biomedical science with mathematical and computational methods. The disputed healthcare placement is excluded from numeric alignment. UCR does not reproduce integrated clinical and medical-engineering training or patient placements.

curriculum.limitation: The external degree requires 180 EC. Official bachelor sources assign the healthcare placement 3.5 or 4.5 EC; it is excluded from the 176.5 EC shown. No balancing adjustment or settled placement weight is assumed.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: All shown components have supported weights; relationships assess biomedical and technical subjects without equating integrated clinical training.
comparisonScope.excluded: The disputed healthcare placement is excluded from numeric alignment. UCR does not reproduce integrated clinical and medical-engineering training or patient placements.

alternatives.label: Biomedical science with mathematical and computational methods
alternatives.concept: Study human anatomy, physiology, disease and pharmacology alongside mathematical modelling, signals, programming and data/image analysis. Product design and robotics provide complementary technical methods. This composition does not reproduce integrated medical-engineering training, patient placements or professional clinical preparation.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the completed curricular composition and the explicitly limited academic claim.
progression: Actual workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites checked for all six fixed terms. Advisory progression considered; no extra hard prerequisites inferred.

candidates.label: Clinical practice, patient communication and medical safety

selection.assessment: The strongest response already combines the supported biomedical and computational strands. A separately organised medical-device/biomechanics programme would need sustained engineering teaching beyond consumer product design and robot manipulation. Clinical-practice/patient-safety inquiry lacks the taught clinical sequence and placements. Both fail substantive feasibility; no second or third option is manufactured.

blocks: Cellular and molecular foundations overlap; the integrated external systems framing is broader.
Neurobiology directly addresses the nervous-system part; engineering signal analysis is separate.
Functional musculoskeletal anatomy is a direct part of the external unit; the engineering biomechanics is not reproduced.
Blood-cell analysis and laboratory immune/microbial methods address identifiable blood/defence content; integrated clinical training differs.
Cardiovascular and respiratory physiology overlap directly; the external medical-engineering integration differs.
Metabolism and biochemical mechanisms overlap the digestive-science part; engineering thermodynamics remains a gap.
Case-based disease, diagnostic and treatment reasoning overlaps; the external clinical-technology integration is not reproduced.
Signals, transforms and system analysis address a specific mathematical-method relationship; wave physics and full integrated scope are not equated.
Probability and statistical inference address the statistics strand only; urogenital-system content is not supplied by this mathematical course.
Python programming addresses the explicit programming part; the combined external mathematics is not equated with this course.
Image filtering, segmentation and recognition address specific processing methods; UCR does not establish medical acquisition or clinical interpretation training.
